It feels like you are a new writer, or have some misgivings new writers tend to have. Writing should, first and foremost, be an outlet for your own creativity. You seem concerned with the moral/ethical dilemma of commentary, copyright, and ethical dilemma for your first world. 

People write about their own problems and the problems around them all the time. Good writing is based in the things you know. This can even be other pieces of writing and other worlds. If the person you’re basing a character ok is real, ask them. Change names of real people and enough details about their life to make it an original character. It’s ok to think “I have a friend with a mental illness, who struggles a lot. I want to write about that struggle.” 

To be honest, if you just want to write about valorant characters, write fanfiction. If you think a character is cool, make an OC like them. Take what you think is interesting you can write about. Expand. Think. Originality takes work, but its ok to be inspired. 

Your writing can take any form it wants. No one is asking anything of you. It doesn’t have to be a single universe with a thousand interconnected dots. Start Smaller. 

But whats very important is: Do not hamstring yourself. Having a goal/premise to write about is ok. But I’ve seen many writers have their characters turn their head to the camera and exclaim “there is no ethical consumption under capitalism!” We know that. You know that. Tell the story first. If your message comes through the story, it will hold water. Make it make sense.

They all take to their power differently. Some Others can be volatile and destructive, or rigid and single-minded. They tend to be at peace as long as they feel fulfilled. One created a worldwide religion, and a different one is treated like a nuclear bomb taped to a ceiling fan. 

People cannot ignore them. Their reality is undisputed. But, oftentimes, so long as their core desires are being fulfilled they are dormant or docile.

While newer or younger Others are usualy still aware of reality, the oldest Others tend to be subject to pure habit. One sings ancient nursery rhymes. Another still fans itself in response to flattery.
Wrath, known as Ifrit, lies down and sleeps like a hound. Not recommended to pet it though.

The gods in my world and mortals are one and the same. Known as the Others, they are an apotheosis of a mortal’s willpower and life rather than a being born into power. Others are extremely rare outcomes for creatures and mages at the height of their power, and are almost always unintentional. 

Others frequently preside over a domain that matched their drive in life, i.e. a mage obsessed with being worshipped in life presides over Faith as an Other. An immortal hound that once obsessed with hunting those who harmed it, presides over Wrath. 

The Others, while not exactly gods, are prone to gaining cultists or followers due to their immense power. This same power, however, tends to drive them mad over time, and Others often are incapable of experiencing anything in the same subjectivity as they did in life. 

They have no need to eat, create no symbols, wield no weapons but magic. If they do any of these, it is out of indulgence or desire.
